transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve felt this heavy, low mood every day for over a year, like I just can’t shake feeling down no matter what I do. It just feels like a constant weight that I can't get away from. A coworker finally convinced me that I needed to come in and talk to someone.
To help me understand, has this low mood been going on continuously for at least two years, or did it start more recently than that?

No, it hasn't been two years, but it has been going on pretty steadily for a little over a year now. It really started shortly after my wife took our son to stay at her sister's house, and it's just been a constant, daily struggle since then.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of deep sadness or depression earlier in your life, before this current episode started a year ago?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before. This is the first time in my life that I have felt this kind of deep sadness or depression. It's all completely new to me, which makes it even harder to deal with.
Along with this constant low mood, have you noticed a significant loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, absolutely. I used to be the guy organizing pickup basketball and grilling out every weekend, but now even the thought of seeing friends or planning anything feels completely exhausting and pointless. I just end up making excuses and sitting on the couch flipping through TV channels without really caring about what's on.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since this low mood started a year ago?

Yes, both have been really bad. I lie awake for hours and then wake up around 3 or 4 AM with my mind racing, leaving me completely exhausted during the day. I've also lost my appetite entirely, skipping meals to the point where I've lost a lot of weight and my coworkers have commented on how gaunt I look.
During this past year, have you also been struggling with feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or any thoughts of self-harm or that life is not worth living?

Yes, I constantly feel like a terrible husband and father who ruined his family, and I'm convinced they'd all be better off without me. It's gotten so bad that, late at night, I've caught myself counting my leftover pain pills and wondering if taking them all would be the easiest way to let everyone move on.
Have you also found it difficult to concentrate, make decisions, or focus on daily tasks since this started?

Yes, my brain feels like it's constantly full of fog. Simple things like writing a work email, analyzing a sales report, or even deciding what to make for dinner take forever because I just can't focus or make up my mind. I also keep forgetting what I was just about to do.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt the exact opposite—such as feeling unusually high, bursting with energy, or needing very little sleep for days?
No, I've never experienced anything like that or felt "high" or full of energy. It's really only been this heavy, low, and exhausted state that I've been describing to you.
Do you have any medical conditions, or are you currently taking any medications, alcohol, or other substances that might be contributing to these feelings?
No, I don't have any major medical conditions, and I'm not taking any regular prescription medications. I also don't really drink much or use drugs, so I don't think any substances are causing this.
